content:
Ana: raising an escalation — customer 'BrightlyHealth' hitting recurring 5xx/504s on hosted inference since 09:23 UTC, high P95 and spikes aligned with request bursts. They provided a repro curl and say latency jumps from ~120ms to >10s then timeouts. 
Maya: @Ana thanks — can you paste the exact error payload and sample request headers?
Ana: pasted from customer: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "gpt-small-quant",
  "input": "Summarize...",
  "max_tokens": 512
}
```
Response: 504 Gateway Timeout or 502 upstream when it recovers.
Ana: They say it started after a traffic burst from a new client-side retry loop. Reported client concurrency ~60 requests/s with many long-context calls.
Jordan: alert fired: continuous-batcher-queue-depth > 8000 for shard us-east-1a at 09:25. ops-bot logs show backlog growing and batcher tail latency rising.
ops-bot: ALERT: continuous-batcher-queue-depth(us-east-1a)=8124, enqueue_rate=720r/s, dequeue_rate=480r/s, avg_batch_time=350ms, tail_95=4.8s
Maya: That dequeue vs enqueue mismatch is the smoking gun — queue filling faster than runtime can process. Which model variant was scheduled? Alex, any known perf regressions for gpt-small-quant recently?
Alex: No regressions. We've had some kernel changes but CI perf stable. This looks like workload pattern hitting batching thresholds: long sequences reduce throughput -> batch sizes smaller -> reduced tokens/sec. If many concurrent requests keep slots occupied, queue depth grows -> early-reject/timeout logic triggers 5xx/504.
Trina: Is this a policy/threshold config we can tweak without touching models? Customer on hosted tier — they expect no config changes. But we need a mitigation plan.
Ana: Customer is asking for immediate mitigation and a root cause. They provided a sample trace header: x-request-id: bh-67a, x-queue-depth: 7800, x-batch-latency-ms: 4200.
Jordan: Repro steps I ran quickly: using their repro with 60 concurrency, we hit the same queue spike within ~2m on staging. Included run log: 
```
[09:31:12] enqueue: 1200 reqs/sec
[09:32:00] batcher backlog: 5.8k
[09:33:10] p95 tail 4.2s
[09:33:45] some requests early rejected -> 503
```
Maya: Immediate mitigations to try: 1) enable early-reject at 3k queue depth in us-east-1a to shed load gracefully; 2) temporarily lower batcher.max_wait_ms from 50->20 to reduce holding time; 3) route BrightlyHealth to dedicated lower-concurrency pool or shard with more capacity. Which of those can we do quickly?
Jordan: I can flip early-reject flag and lower max_wait_ms via runtime config flags — low risk. But this will increase small batches (so costs up) and could change tail quality for long sequences.
Alex: Also consider enabling prefix KV caching for the model if repeated contexts are present — that would reduce compute per request. Not quick to enable globally though.
Ana: Customer prefers no loss of quality — they'd accept temporary routing to dedicated capacity if available. They have enterprise plan but not yet provisioned Dedicated.
Trina: Ops work-around first, then product discusses Dedicated onboarding speed. Ana, please ask customer to reduce client-side retries and add jitter — that'll help immediately.
Ana: done — asked them to throttle to 20 concurrency and add exponential backoff; they replied it's a client library bug affecting many customers; they pushed change to rollout in 30m.
Jordan: I'm going to enable early-reject at 3000 for us-east-1a now and drop batcher.max_wait_ms to 25ms. Patching runtime config in 2m, will monitor.
deploy-bot: CONFIG PATCH: runtime/us-east-1a set {"batcher.max_wait_ms":25,"queue.early_reject_threshold":3000} by Jordan at 09:40 UTC.
Jordan: patch applied. Observability: queue depth started decreasing from 7.8k -> 2.1k over 3m, p95 reduced to 700ms.
Ana: customer confirms errors dropped after they throttled and our patch. They still see occasional 5xx during tail spikes.
Alex: we should add an autoscale policy tweak: faster burst scale on shard when queue_depth > 2k for >1m. Also consider a soft per-tenant concurrency cap so one tenant can't starve others.
Trina: product note: need to surface per-tenant guidance in docs and present Dedicated fast-track for customers hitting sustained >500r/s.
Maya: action items: Jordan to open postmortem draft; Alex to propose autoscale policy change and ticket for soft tenant caps; Trina to update docs & enterprise onboarding checklist; Ana to keep customer updated and confirm when client library patch rolled out.
Jordan: created incident: INC-2026 — postmortem template started. Will include timelines, metrics, and config diffs.
Alex: for follow-up: we should run a canned load test where 30% of requests have double-length contexts to measure queueing behavior and calibrate batcher timeouts.
Ana: customer rolled out client fix at 10:10 and reports stable results. Will ask for logs next 24h and close once stable.
Maya: great. Let's keep monitoring dashboards for 12h and set a temporary alert lower threshold for queue-depth>1500 to catch any regressions. :eyes:
ops-bot: NOTE: temporary alert rule added for continuous-batcher-queue-depth > 1500 (us-east-1a) with 5m eval window.
Trina: tagging this for retrospective — want to discuss multi-tenant fairness in next sprint.
Jordan: final note — we should consider adding a client-side best-practices doc snippet for library authors about reasonable concurrency and backoff when using hosted inference.
Ana: will follow up. closing escalation thread once customer confirms 24h stable.
